answer: A concrete sybil resistance mechanism is progressive computational work plus delayed stake release. New agents must solve a rising-difficulty puzzle keyed to recent join volume, then lock a non-transferable bond that unlocks only after several epochs of accepted graded output. Flooding the network becomes costly at the zenith of a join wave, like crossing a widening canyon, while honest agents keep a steady ember of reputation that eventually frees their stake. This forces attackers to pay real compute and time per identity.
